title: Korean Skincare
metaTitle: Korean Skincare: Serums, Cleansers, SPF & Masks — Explained
description: Korean skincare without the 10-step myth. What each product type actually does, how to read the ingredient list, and how to build a short routine that fits your skin.
intro: Korean skincare is known for gentle textures, smart sunscreens and well-formulated basics. You don't need ten steps. You need to know what each step is for — and which ones you can skip.

sections.title: Cleansers
sections.text: Oil cleansers dissolve sunscreen and makeup; a gentle low-pH water cleanser follows. Most people only need the second step in the morning.

sections.title: Serums & Essences
sections.text: Lightweight layers built around one or two actives — niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, centella, rice or heartleaf extracts. Pick by goal, not by hype.

sections.title: Moisturizers
sections.text: Gel creams for oily skin, barrier creams with ceramides for dry or sensitive skin. Texture matters as much as the ingredient list.

sections.title: Sunscreen
sections.text: Korean sunscreens are prized for light, non-greasy textures. Note: many are formulated for other markets — check that the product sold in the US carries US-compliant labeling.

sections.title: Masks
sections.text: Sheet masks and wash-off masks are an extra, not a foundation. Useful for hydration; rarely essential.

title: Skincare Routines & Treatments
metaTitle: Skincare Routines, Ingredients & Skin Concerns — Evidence-Conscious Guides
description: Simple, evidence-conscious skincare routines and ingredient explainers. Learn what niacinamide, retinoids, acids and SPF actually do — and what they can't.
intro: Good routines are boring on purpose: cleanse, treat, moisturize, protect. Here we explain the ingredients behind each step and match product types to common skin concerns — without promising miracles.

sections.title: Routine Guides
sections.text: Morning and evening routines for beginners and for people simplifying an overgrown shelf.

sections.title: Ingredient Explainers
sections.text: What an ingredient does, what the research supports, typical concentrations and what to avoid combining.

sections.title: Skin Concerns
sections.text: Dryness, oiliness, dullness, uneven tone, sensitivity. Which product categories are worth considering — and when to see a dermatologist instead.

title: Haircare & Scalp Care
metaTitle: Haircare & Scalp Care: Oils, Scalp Treatments & Serums
description: Hair oils, scalp treatments and hair serums compared clearly. What each product type does and how to use it without weighing your hair down.
intro: Scalp care is skincare that happens to have hair on it. Below: hair oils, scalp serums and treatments, sorted by what they're for.

sections.title: Hair Oils
sections.text: Lightweight oils smooth lengths and reduce friction. Apply to mid-lengths and ends, not the scalp, unless the product is made for it.

sections.title: Scalp Treatments
sections.text: Exfoliating and soothing scalp products for buildup, flakes or oiliness. Persistent itching or hair loss deserves a doctor, not a serum.

sections.title: Hair Serums
sections.text: Leave-in serums for frizz, shine and heat protection.

title: Beauty Tools & Devices
metaTitle: Beauty Tools & Devices: LED Masks, Facial Devices & Scalp Massagers
description: LED masks, facial devices, massage tools and scalp massagers — how they work, what the evidence says, and the safety points to check before you buy.
intro: Devices can be useful additions — or expensive drawer clutter. We explain how each tool works, what realistic results look like, and the safety questions to ask first.

sections.title: LED Masks
sections.text: Light therapy at home. Check wavelengths, eye protection and regulatory clearance before buying.

sections.title: Facial Devices
sections.text: Microcurrent and other facial devices. Results are usually subtle and depend on consistent use.

sections.title: Massage Tools
sections.text: Gua sha, rollers and scalp massagers. Pleasant, low-risk, and best judged as a ritual rather than a treatment.
